data.title: Middle East Eye: Manchester City chief claims 'conspiracy' as UAE-owned club found guilty of financial violations charges
data.author: Fleur Hargreaves
data.summary:
Manchester City chief claims 'conspiracy' as UAE-owned club found guilty of financial violations charges
An independent commission on Tuesday revealed that Manchester City Football Club has been found guilty on all 115 charges related to financial rules violations.
The club engaged in "sham" commercial contracts to artificially inflate revenues and reduce costs by more than $1bn, the findings showed.
"The Club’s financial statements had not been prepared and audited in accordance with applicable legal and regulatory principles," the commission wrote.
It was "reckless" and "acted other than with utmost good faith", it added.
In a video sent to staff and players and obtained by Sky Sports News, City's chief executive, Ferran Soriano, called the investigation a "Premier League conspiracy theory".
Read more: Manchester City chief claims 'conspiracy' as UAE-owned club found guilty of financial violations charges

data.title: Middle East Eye: Saudi Arabia turns to UAE 'white horse' as it gears up to battle Yemen's Houthis
data.author: Mera Aladam
data.summary:
Saudi Arabia turns to UAE 'white horse' as it gears up to battle Yemen's Houthis
Saudi Arabia appears to be mending fences with the UAE in an effort to push back a Houthi military offensive in Yemen that threatens the kingdom’s Red Sea oil export corridor and has seen drones strike Riyadh.
Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman hosted the UAE’s Vice President, Mansour Bin Zayed, in Riyadh on Tuesday, marking the kingdom's most prominent effort yet to reconcile with the UAE after clashing over Sudan, Yemen, and Somaliland.
“The Houthis are bringing Saudi Arabia and the UAE closer together,” Anna Jacobs, a non-resident fellow at the Arab Gulf States Institute, told Middle East Eye.
The two neighbours have been discussing how to collaborate on Yemen for months, western and Arab officials tell MEE, but the talks have been moving slowly.

data.author: Fleur Hargreaves
data.summary:
US Treasury Secretary says economic action against Iran to continue
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Tuesday that the economic measures against Iran will continue, targeting those providing financial support to Iran.
“Under Operation Economic Outcast, Treasury will continue to target and disrupt those who provide material, technological, or financial support that allows the Iranian regime to sustain its terrorist enterprise,” Bessent said.
“Treasury will not tolerate any support to the regime and will continue to identify, expose, and isolate Iran’s enablers,” he added.
Meanwhile, US State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott highlighted on Tuesday a $15m reward offered by the US government for information that disrupts the financial mechanisms of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).

data.title: Middle East Eye: Qatar's prime minister calls Netanyahu 'war criminal', says Doha will continue diplomacy efforts in region
data.author: Mera Aladam
data.summary:
Qatar's prime minister calls Netanyahu 'war criminal', says Doha will continue diplomacy efforts in region
Qatar's prime minister accused his Israeli counterpart, Benjamin Netanyahu, of being a "war criminal", and stressed that Doha would continue its mediation efforts despite escalating tensions in the region.
During an interview with Piers Morgan, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani - who is also Qatar's foreign minister - was asked whether he considered Netanyahu a war criminal.
Sheikh Mohammad responded by saying: "Of course. What’s been committed in Gaza is war crimes, and whoever is responsible for this is a war criminal."
"Hospitals have been targeted, schools have been targeted. Whatever the justifications and the arguments, nothing is justifying this," he added.
He also brought up Israel's attack on Qatar in early September of last year, when it targeted Hamas officials while Doha was engaged in mediation efforts.
"We were attacked by Israel while we were mediating," he said. "Netanyahu has crossed the line like he has crossed other lines before that."
Despite escalating regional tensions, Sheikh Mohammed indicated Qatar's readiness in ongoing diplomacy and mediation efforts.
"We are trying to do our best to give the best advice to the US government on how to reach a solution, as well as to the Iranians," he said.

Iran warns Israel's presence is creating a 'dangerous situation', condemns Netanyahu’s visit to UAE
Iran's foreign ministry warned on Tuesday that Israel's presence in the region was creating a "dangerous situation", after Benjamin Netanyahu’s visit to the UAE was confirmed.
The ministry slammed the visit, saying it came at a "sensitive time" amid ongoing Israeli attacks on Iran, Lebanon and Palestine.
It added that Israel’s presence in the region was creating a "dangerous situation", calling on regional countries to remain alert to threats to collective peace and security.
The ministry also reiterated Iran's previous warnings to the region against allowing their territory to be used for actions that could undermine stability.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Israel's opposition leader accuses Netanyahu of fearmongering ahead of elections
data.author: Mera Aladam
data.summary:
Israel's opposition leader accuses Netanyahu of fearmongering ahead of elections
Israeli opposition leader Yair Lapid accused Benjamin Netanyahu of stoking security fears, claiming that enemies might attack ahead of the 27 October elections.
Lapid reportedly requested an urgent security briefing after Netanyahu on Tuesday said that there were "indications" that Israel’s enemies could try to attack the country before elections began.
The prime minister's claims came during a visit to Tel Nof Airbase in central Israel.
"Netanyahu ignored every warning before October 7 and now, 28 days before the election, he’s suddenly busy fearmongering," Lapid said.
After the meeting late on Tuesday, Lapid asserted that "there is no reason to panic the public", adding that Israeli military bases "are not the setting for election videos".
"I of course will not violate the confidentiality of the security briefing but it must be said - security threats must be handled professionally and responsibly," Lapid said.
